questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:

options.text: There are only a few vehicles on the road.
Drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.explanation: You need more space to stop on a slippery road. Increase your following distance if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see around the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: The best lane position:

options.text: Is always on the right side of the lane.
Is always in the center of the lane.
Is always on the left side of the lane.
Changes based on the road, weather, and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes based on the road, weather, and traffic.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position in the lane based on road conditions, weather, and traffic.

questions.question: An effective eye or face shield should have all of these features except:
questions.explanation: A good eye shield or face shield must be scratch-free, resist breaking, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and fit over eyeglasses. It does not need to be airtight.

questions.question: A rider in your group wants to ride faster than everyone else. What should the group do?

options.text: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a set location later.
Speed up to match the faster rider.
Split up and let each rider go their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a set location later.
questions.explanation: If one rider wants to go faster than the rest, let them ride ahead alone. Plan to meet at a designated spot later.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps others see you at all times. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so wear bright clothing during daylight hours too.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are rectangular with white background and black letters. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: A dog is chasing you on your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Slow down near the dog, then speed up quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down near the dog, then speed up quickly.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, slow down and approach the dog. Once you are close, accelerate and leave it behind. Do not try to kick the dog.

questions.question: Your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
Grip the handlebars tightly and speed up to cross quickly.
Move to the shoulder to avoid the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is normal and not dangerous. Stay relaxed, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across. Zigzagging is more dangerous.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect like:
questions.explanation: When you downshift to a lower gear, your motorcycle slows down.

questions.question: Where do motorcycle operators face the greatest conflict with other drivers?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcyclists have the most conflicts with other drivers. Use extra caution when entering and crossing intersections.

questions.question: If your motorcycle chain or belt breaks, what happens?

options.text: The rear wheel suddenly gains power.
The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly gains power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
questions.explanation: If your chain or belt breaks, the rear wheel will lose power right away.

questions.question: When riding at night, how should you change your following distance compared to daytime riding?

options.text: Stay farther back from other vehicles at night.
Stay closer to other vehicles at night.
Keep the same distance at all times of day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back from other vehicles at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distances because you lose visual cues like shadows and light. You should always stay farther back from other vehicles at night than during the day.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Skip the jacket if it is warm outside.
Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
Do not worry about loose shoelaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket made of appropriate material when riding, even in warm weather. It helps protect you and prevent dehydration. Also wear long pants and tuck in your shoelaces so they do not catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is usually on the right handlebar. Learn where all your motorcycle controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: What makes a motorcycle a moped?

options.text: The seat is less than 15 inches off the ground.
It produces no more than five brake horsepower.
It does not have a seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: It produces no more than five brake horsepower.
questions.explanation: A moped is defined as a motorcycle, motor scooter, or motorized bicycle that produces no more than five brake horsepower and has a seat at least 26 inches from the ground.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts out.
